# They label the 1000 rows sampled by iteration 8 in docs/measurements/engineering-role-2026-09-28.md.
# Labelled on 2026-09-22 from docs/engineering-role-criterion.md alone, at revision
# db5e80b87e890df24684a54257fb2688b675188d, over the bare cleaned titles, before any rule of the
# classifier was read.
# Labelled by a subagent denied the classifier's source, the iteration reports and the earlier
# label fixtures; it read the criterion and the sample and nothing else.
# This fixture is never regenerated: a session is not reproducible, so the labels are the artifact
# and not the process that made them.
# Families labelled under criterion rules a future revision might supersede:
#   - architect as a domain-free head: building-architecture titles (Hospitality Architect,
#     Architect Justice+Civic) are UNKNOWN/domain_ambiguity here, not OUT, because the criterion
#     calls architect domain-free and market markers settle nothing under a domain-free head.
#   - the market-marker rule at step 6: engineer titles whose only modifier names a market
#     (Commercial Sales Engineer, Trading Operations Engineer) are OUT, even where the work may
#     well be software.
#   - consultant as domain-bound (the criterion's own reclass): every consultant title with a
#     non-software modifier is OUT.
#   - designer heads (Product Designer, User Experience Designer, Gameplay Designer, Technical
#     Designer) are OUT on Q2-Q4, since a software background alone does not make a credible
#     designer; the criterion names no designer head, so a revision could rule this family either way.
#   - firmware and network heads (Firmware Engineer, SSD Firmware Engineer, Network Engineer,
#     NOC Engineer) are IN here, read as code and engineer-facing artifacts rather than as a
#     hardware credential; the FPGA/ASIC discipline argument could be extended to them instead.
